thesis: Buying a small-cap, still loss-making med-tech name into a risk-off tape (VIX percentile 0.981, QQQ below its 50- and 200-day) is poor timing, because high-beta small caps tend to get sold hard when the market breaks down. The stock is only 4.4% below its 52-week high, and the analyst mean target (26.78) sits barely above the 24.77 close. The technical card's own reward/risk of 1.77 is called mediocre because resistance at 25.92 is close. The rally rests on one gap-up on the Q3 10-Q, with growth stable rather than accelerating and sequential revenue slightly down. Insiders (CEO, CLO and another officer) sold into strength, and 11.7% short interest plus a +69% six-month run make a sharp reversal toward the 20-day SMA and swing low plausible.
